waivers.text:
SLEEPER — FAAB: $87 of $100 remaining. Waivers process this week — get claims in today. Top 5:
1. Mike Gesicki (TE, CIN) — FAAB $9. Still unclaimed from Tuesday's recommendation — resubmit now before it's gone. Noah Fant left for New Orleans, Gesicki's the clear top receiving TE in Cincinnati, ran a route on the highest snap rate of any NFL TE last year. Drop Darnell Washington (buried PIT TE2).
2. Dohnte Meyers (WR, CIN) — FAAB $4. New add — #2 most-added player league-wide the last 24 hours. He's Cincinnati's clear WR3 behind Chase and Higgins with Andrei Iosivas on IR, and direct insurance given Higgins' recurring injury flags (adductor strain, unresolved as of this morning). Drop Woody Marks (buried Houston RB3).
3. Cleveland DEF — FAAB $3. Still available. Your real problem is Week 7: JAX (your only DEF), LAC (Herbert/Hampton), and WAS (Diggs) are all on bye the same week — Cleveland is a soft Week 7 stream. Lower priority than Gesicki/Meyers; grab if FAAB allows.
4. Deshaun Watson (QB, CLE) — FAAB $2, speculative. Pure depth behind Herbert/Shough given the QB slot has been mismanaged repeatedly this season. Only if you have a free bench spot after the above.
5. Michael Mayer (TE, LV) — FAAB $1, speculative. Backup plan only if the Gesicki claim fails.
Heads up: Will Shipley (last week's #2 target) is gone — your Week 5 opponent (Weak Homie Quon) grabbed him first. Don't chase him again.

YAHOO — still no free-agent visibility (private league, no login) and the newest screenshot in your Drive folder is still from Sept 13 (now 24 days old). I can't verify Yahoo waivers this week — drop a fresh screenshot of the free-agent pool if you want real bid guidance there. Two things worth your own look in the meantime: Blake Corum's ceiling is capped by a near-even timeshare with Kyren Williams, not a clean workhorse role; and Tank Bigsby (your own bench RB) is out til at least Week 9 post core-muscle surgery — drop him for anything you need the spot for.

season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.

Tyler Shough (22.38, waiver QB stash) outscored started QB Justin Herbert (9.88) by 12.5 — not a real swap given Shough's a Saints starter you don't play, but the bigger miss was starting Michael Wilson (3.8) over bench WR Josh Downs (14.2), a 10.4-point gap; the Week 3 lineup already has that fixed. Also: Zay Flowers stayed rostered through a scoreless Week 2 (ruled Out, no IR move) — a wasted bench spot two weeks running.

Michael Wilson (25.9) outscored started Josh Downs (12.7) by 13.2 on the bench — the second straight week a bench WR beat a starter by double digits. Backup QB Tyler Shough (24.8) also beat Herbert (13.74) again. Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — that exact overcorrection sat live in your Week 4 lineup for five straight days (Shough over Herbert) until this run flagged it again.

Left the QB slot completely empty all week (Shough would've scored 15.94 sitting there unused) and started Josh Downs (4.6) over Omarion Hampton (13.3) in the flex — an 8.7-point unforced error stacked on a totally wasted roster slot. A win over a weak opponent papered over the worst bench-management week of the season so far; double-check every single slot is filled before Thursday lock, every week, no exceptions.
